learn: "Hola" means hello. "Adiós" means goodbye. "Hasta luego" means see you later.
"Buenos días" is good morning, "buenas tardes" is good afternoon and "buenas noches" is good evening or good night.
In many Spanish-speaking countries, friends greet with a handshake, a hug or a kiss on the cheek.
lessons.try: Greet three classmates in Spanish using the right time of day.

learn: "¿Cómo te llamas?" means "What is your name?" Answer: "Me llamo..." (My name is...).
"Mucho gusto" means "Nice to meet you."
"¿De dónde eres?" means "Where are you from?" Answer: "Soy de..." (I am from...).
lessons.try: Introduce yourself to a partner with your name and where you are from.

learn: "¿Cómo estás?" means "How are you?" (to a friend). "¿Cómo está usted?" is the polite form.
Answers: "Bien" (well), "Muy bien" (very well), "Así así" (so-so), "Mal" (bad).
Polite words: "por favor" (please), "gracias" (thank you), "de nada" (you're welcome).
check: The polite way to ask an adult "how are you" is...
lessons.try: Act out a short conversation asking how someone is.

learn: "¿De dónde eres?" means "Where are you from?"
Answer: "Soy de..." (I am from...).
"Soy de Arizona" means "I am from Arizona."
lessons.try: Ask three classmates where they are from.

learn: Use "tú" with friends, family and children.
Use "usted" with adults you respect, like teachers.
"¿Cómo está usted?" is the polite "How are you?"
check: With your best friend you use...
lessons.try: Greet a friend and a teacher in the right way.

learn: "Por favor" means please.
"Gracias" means thank you; "de nada" means you're welcome.
"Perdón" or "disculpe" means excuse me.
lessons.try: Role-play asking for a pencil politely.

learn: "¿Cuántos años tienes?" means "How old are you?"
Answer: "Tengo doce años" (I am twelve).
Spanish uses "tener" (to have) for age.
lessons.try: Ask and answer ages with a partner.

learn: Hola, ¿cómo te llamas? Me llamo Ana.
¿De dónde eres? Soy de Tucson.
Mucho gusto. Igualmente. ¡Adiós!
check: The answer to "Mucho gusto" is often...
lessons.try: Perform a meeting dialogue.

learn: Greetings and goodbyes.
Introductions.
Polite words.
lessons.try: Introduce yourself fully in Spanish.

learn: The Spanish alphabet has 27 letters, including ñ (eñe), as in "niño" (boy).
Letters are named differently: a (ah), e (eh), i (ee), o (oh), u (oo).
Spelling your name in Spanish is a useful skill.
lessons.try: Spell your name aloud using Spanish letter names.

learn: Spanish vowels each have one clear sound: a as in "father", e as in "met", i as in "see", o as in "go", u as in "food".
The letter h is always silent: "hola" sounds like "ola".
"ll" sounds like the y in "yes": "llamo". "j" sounds like a strong h: "jugo".
lessons.try: Read a list of Spanish words aloud, focusing on vowels.

learn: Accent marks show which syllable to stress: "teléfono".
Accents can change meaning: "si" (if) and "sí" (yes).
Upside-down marks begin questions and exclamations: ¿...? and ¡...!
lessons.try: Write three questions with correct punctuation.

learn: Ñ sounds like "ny" in canyon.
"Año" means year; "niño" means child.
Without the tilde, "ano" is a different word, so the mark matters.
lessons.try: Find five words with ñ.

learn: H makes no sound in Spanish.
"Hola" sounds like "o-la".
"Hotel" sounds like "o-tel".
lessons.try: Read ten words with a silent h.

learn: J sounds like a strong English h: "jugo".
G before e or i sounds the same: "gente", "gigante".
G before a, o, u is hard: "gato".
check: "Jugo" starts with a sound like English...
lessons.try: Sort words by their g sound.

learn: LL and Y often sound like English y: "llama", "yo".
RR is a rolled r: "perro".
A single r between vowels is a quick tap: "pero".
lessons.try: Practise "perro" and "pero".

learn: "¿Cómo se escribe?" means "How do you spell it?"
Spell your name with Spanish letter names.
Practise with a partner.
lessons.try: Spell your name and two places.

learn: Alphabet.
Vowels.
Accents and stress.
lessons.try: Read a short paragraph aloud.

learn: Uno, dos, tres, cuatro, cinco, seis, siete, ocho, nueve, diez.
Teens: once, doce, trece... Tens: veinte, treinta, cuarenta, cincuenta... cien (100).
Combine tens and ones: treinta y cinco (35).
lessons.try: Count by tens to 100 in Spanish.

learn: Days: lunes, martes, miércoles, jueves, viernes, sábado, domingo.
Months: enero, febrero, marzo, abril, mayo, junio, julio, agosto, septiembre, octubre, noviembre, diciembre.
In Spanish, days and months are not capitalised.
lessons.try: Write this week's days with a Spanish activity for each.

learn: "¿Cuál es la fecha?" means "What is the date?"
Dates go day then month: "Es el cinco de mayo" (It's the 5th of May).
"¿Cuándo es tu cumpleaños?" means "When is your birthday?"
check: In Spanish dates, the day comes...
At the end of the year
lessons.try: Ask three classmates their birthdays in Spanish.

learn: Cien is 100; ciento uno is 101.
Doscientos is 200, quinientos 500.
Mil is 1000.
lessons.try: Read five prices out loud.

learn: Primero, segundo, tercero: first, second, third.
Used for floors and places in a race.
"El primero de mayo" is the first of May.
lessons.try: Rank five classmates in a race in Spanish.

learn: Phone numbers are often said in pairs.
52-14-80 is "cincuenta y dos, catorce, ochenta".
"¿Cuál es tu número de teléfono?"
check: Phone numbers are often said in...
lessons.try: Say a made-up phone number in pairs.

learn: Invierno: diciembre, enero, febrero (in the north).
Seasons are opposite south of the equator.
July is winter in Argentina.
lessons.try: Match months and seasons for two countries.

learn: Days start on lunes in Spanish calendars.
Days and months are not capitalised.
Mark birthdays and holidays.
lessons.try: Make a Spanish calendar page.

lessons.t: Show What You Know: Numbers and Dates
learn: Numbers.
Days and months.
Dates and birthdays.
lessons.try: Say your birthday and age in Spanish.

learn: Rojo (red), azul (blue), amarillo (yellow), verde (green), negro (black), blanco (white), anaranjado (orange), morado (purple).
Colors come after the noun: "el lápiz rojo" (the red pencil).
Some colors change ending to match: "la casa roja" (the red house).
lessons.try: Name the colors of five things in your room.

learn: El libro (book), el cuaderno (notebook), el lápiz (pencil), la mochila (backpack), la mesa (table), la silla (chair).
"El" and "la" both mean "the": el for masculine, la for feminine nouns.
"¿Qué es esto?" means "What is this?"
lessons.try: Label ten objects in your room with Spanish sticky notes.

learn: To make plurals, add -s after a vowel (libros) or -es after a consonant (papeles).
"Los" and "las" are the plural forms of "el" and "la".
"Hay" means "there is" or "there are": "Hay tres libros."
lessons.try: Describe your backpack using "hay".

learn: Colours match the noun: "el libro rojo", "la mesa roja".
Plurals add -s: "los libros rojos".
Verde and azul change only for plural.
lessons.try: Describe ten objects with colours.

learn: Encima de (on top of), debajo de (under).
Al lado de (next to), dentro de (inside).
"El lápiz está debajo de la mesa."
lessons.try: Hide an object and describe where it is.

learn: Abran los libros: open your books.
Escuchen: listen. Repitan: repeat.
Siéntense: sit down.
lessons.try: Play "Simón dice" with commands.

learn: "¿Qué es esto?" means "What is this?"
"Es un borrador." It is an eraser.
"¿Cómo se dice ... en español?"
check: To ask how to say a word:
lessons.try: Ask the name of five objects.

learn: En mi mochila hay un cuaderno.
También hay dos bolígrafos.
No hay tijeras.
lessons.try: List what is in your backpack.

learn: Colours.
Objects.
Plurals and hay.
lessons.try: Describe your classroom in six sentences.

learn: Madre (mother), padre (father), hermano (brother), hermana (sister), abuelo (grandfather), abuela (grandmother).
Tío and tía are uncle and aunt; primo and prima are cousins.
"Tengo dos hermanos" means "I have two brothers (or siblings)."
lessons.try: Draw your family tree with Spanish labels.

learn: Alto (tall), bajo (short), simpático (nice), inteligente (intelligent), divertido (fun).
Adjectives match the person: "Él es alto." "Ella es alta."
Use "muy" for very: "muy simpática".
lessons.try: Describe a family member using three adjectives.

learn: Mi (my), tu (your), su (his/her/their).
"Mi madre" means my mother; "mis hermanos" means my brothers.
Add -s when the noun is plural.
lessons.try: Write five sentences about your family using mi and mis.

learn: Abuelos, tíos, primos: grandparents, uncles and aunts, cousins.
"Mi prima" is a girl cousin.
"Mis primos" can include boys and girls.
lessons.try: Draw and label an extended family tree.

learn: Simpático (nice), inteligente, trabajador (hard-working).
Gracioso (funny), tímido (shy).
Adjectives match gender: simpática.
lessons.try: Describe three family members' personalities.

learn: Alto (tall), bajo (short), pelo castaño (brown hair).
Ojos azules: blue eyes.
"Tiene el pelo largo."
lessons.try: Describe a classmate for others to guess.

learn: Perro (dog), gato (cat), pez (fish).
"Tengo un perro que se llama Max."
Pájaro means bird.
lessons.try: Present a real or made-up pet.

learn: Start with how many people.
Describe each one.
End with what you do together.
check: "En mi familia hay cuatro personas" means...
There are four people in my family
lessons.try: Write a paragraph about your family.

learn: La familia.
Describing people.
Possessives.
lessons.try: Present your family tree.

units.t: The Verb Ser and Subject Pronouns

learn: Yo (I), tú (you, friend), usted (you, polite), él (he), ella (she).
Nosotros (we), ellos (they, masculine or mixed), ellas (they, feminine).
Spanish often drops the pronoun because the verb shows who: "Soy" = I am.
lessons.try: Point to people around you and say the right pronoun.

learn: Ser means "to be" for lasting traits: yo soy, tú eres, él/ella/usted es.
Nosotros somos, ellos/ellas/ustedes son.
Use ser for identity, origin, description and time.
lessons.try: Write a sentence with each form of ser.

learn: Put "no" before the verb: "No soy alto."
Questions can use the same words with rising voice: "¿Eres de México?"
Answer: "Sí, soy de México" or "No, no soy de México."
lessons.try: Ask and answer three yes-or-no questions.

learn: Ser tells where someone is from.
"Ellos son de Perú."
"¿De dónde son ustedes?"
check: "Ellos son de Perú": the subject is...
lessons.try: Say where five famous people were from.

learn: "Ella es doctora." No "una" needed.
Profesor, profesora; ingeniero, ingeniera.
"¿Qué es tu madre?"
check: Before a profession after ser, Spanish usually ___ "un" or "una".
lessons.try: Name five jobs in Spanish.

learn: "Es la una." It is one o'clock.
"Son las tres." It is three.
"Hoy es lunes."
lessons.try: Tell the time of three classes.

learn: Vosotros is "you all" in Spain.
Latin America uses ustedes.
"Vosotros sois" vs "ustedes son".
check: Latin America uses ___ for you all.
lessons.try: Rewrite three sentences for Spain.

learn: Add question marks at both ends: ¿...?
Raise your voice at the end.
"¿Eres estudiante?"
lessons.try: Write five yes/no questions.

learn: Pronouns.
Conjugation.
Negatives.
lessons.try: Write ten sentences with ser.

learn: Matemáticas, ciencias, historia, inglés, arte, música, educación física.
"Mi clase favorita es arte" means "My favourite class is art."
"Me gusta" means "I like": "Me gusta la música."
lessons.try: Make a list of your classes in Spanish and star your favourite.

learn: "¿Qué hora es?" means "What time is it?"
"Es la una" (It's 1:00). "Son las tres" (It's 3:00). "Son las cuatro y media" (4:30).
"¿A qué hora es la clase?" asks what time the class is.
lessons.try: Draw five clocks and write the time in Spanish.

learn: Por la mañana (in the morning), por la tarde (in the afternoon).
"Tengo matemáticas a las nueve" means "I have maths at nine."
Describe your schedule with times and subjects.
lessons.try: Write your school-day schedule in Spanish.

learn: La biblioteca (library), el gimnasio (gym).
La cafetería, el laboratorio.
"Voy a la biblioteca."
lessons.try: Draw a school map with labels.

learn: De la mañana: in the morning (a.m.).
De la tarde: in the afternoon.
De la noche: at night.
check: "A las ocho de la mañana" means at 8...
lessons.try: Say when your classes are with times of day.

learn: "Me gusta el arte porque es divertido."
Difícil, fácil, interesante, aburrido.
Porque means because.
lessons.try: Give opinions about four classes.

learn: "Necesito un cuaderno."
"¿Cuánto cuesta?"
"Cuesta dos dólares."
lessons.try: Role-play buying supplies.

learn: Many students wear uniforms.
Some schools have morning and afternoon shifts.
Grades often go from 1 to 10 or 1 to 20.
check: Many students in Spanish-speaking countries wear...
Some schools have morning and afternoon...
Grades may be marked out of...
lessons.try: Compare a school day in another country with yours.

learn: Subjects.
Telling time.
My school day.
lessons.try: Present your weekly schedule.

learn: El pan (bread), el queso (cheese), la manzana (apple), el arroz (rice), el pollo (chicken), el agua (water), la leche (milk), el jugo (juice).
Meals: el desayuno (breakfast), el almuerzo (lunch), la cena (dinner).
"Tengo hambre" means "I'm hungry"; "Tengo sed" means "I'm thirsty."
lessons.try: Write your favourite breakfast in Spanish.

learn: "Quisiera..." means "I would like..." "Para mí, una ensalada" means "For me, a salad."
"¿Cuánto cuesta?" means "How much does it cost?"
"La cuenta, por favor" means "The bill, please."
lessons.try: Role-play ordering lunch at a café with a partner.

learn: "Me gusta el chocolate" (I like chocolate). "Me gustan las uvas" (I like grapes: plural).
"No me gusta" means "I don't like".
"¿Te gusta...?" asks "Do you like...?"
check: "Me gustan las uvas" uses gustan because uvas is...
lessons.try: Survey classmates about foods they like and dislike.

learn: El desayuno (breakfast), el almuerzo (lunch), la cena (dinner).
In Spain, lunch is often the big meal.
Dinner can be late, at 9 or 10 p.m.
check: In Spain, the big meal is often...
lessons.try: Describe what you eat at each meal.

learn: Manzana (apple), plátano (banana), naranja (orange).
Zanahoria (carrot), lechuga (lettuce).
Fresa means strawberry.
lessons.try: Make a Spanish shopping list.

learn: "Un kilo de tomates, por favor."
"¿Algo más?" Anything else?
"Nada más, gracias."
lessons.try: Role-play buying at a market stall.

learn: Tacos and tamales from Mexico.
Paella from Spain.
Arepas from Venezuela and Colombia.
lessons.try: Research a dish and its country.

learn: "La cuenta, por favor." The bill, please.
Tipping customs vary by country.
"¿Aceptan tarjetas?"
lessons.try: Act out paying at a café.

learn: Foods and drinks.
Ordering.
Likes and dislikes.
lessons.try: Order a full meal in Spanish.

learn: An infinitive is the basic form of a verb, like "hablar" (to speak).
Spanish infinitives end in -ar, -er or -ir.
Common -ar verbs: hablar, estudiar, bailar, cantar, caminar, escuchar.
lessons.try: List ten -ar verbs with their English meanings.

learn: Drop -ar and add endings: yo -o, tú -as, él/ella -a, nosotros -amos, ellos -an.
Hablar: hablo, hablas, habla, hablamos, hablan.
"Yo estudio español" means "I study Spanish."
lessons.try: Conjugate "cantar" in all forms.

learn: "¿Escuchas música?" (Do you listen to music?) "Sí, escucho música."
Add time words: siempre (always), a veces (sometimes), nunca (never).
Write sentences about your weekly routine.
lessons.try: Write five sentences about what you do after school.

learn: Bailar (dance), cantar (sing), nadar (swim).
Escuchar (listen), mirar (watch).
Trabajar (work), estudiar (study).
lessons.try: Act out verbs for others to guess.

learn: Siempre (always), a veces (sometimes), nunca (never).
Todos los días: every day.
"Nunca canto en clase."
lessons.try: Say how often you do five things.

learn: "¿Hablas español?"
"¿Dónde trabajan tus padres?"
Question words: dónde, cuándo, qué.
lessons.try: Interview a partner with -ar verbs.

learn: "El sábado, monto en bicicleta."
"Los domingos, descanso."
Los + day means every that day.
lessons.try: Describe your weekend routine.

learn: Read a paragraph about a student's week.
Find each -ar verb.
Answer questions in Spanish.
check: In "Ana estudia mucho," the verb is...
lessons.try: Read and answer five questions.

learn: Infinitives.
Conjugation.
Sentences.
lessons.try: Write about your week with ten -ar verbs.

learn: Spanish is an official language in 20 countries, including Spain, Mexico, Argentina, Colombia and Peru.
Over 500 million people speak Spanish, and many millions live in the United States.
Spanish came from Latin, the language of ancient Rome.
lessons.try: Colour Spanish-speaking countries on a world map.

learn: Día de los Muertos (Day of the Dead) in Mexico honours loved ones who have died with altars, flowers and food.
La Tomatina in Spain is a tomato-throwing festival.
Many countries celebrate their independence days with parades and music.
check: Independence days are often celebrated with...
lessons.try: Research a festival from a Spanish-speaking country and present it.

learn: Spanish-speaking cultures gave the world flamenco, salsa, tango and mariachi music.
Foods include tacos, paella, empanadas and arepas.
Learning a language opens doors to new friends and cultures.
check: Learning a language opens doors to...
lessons.try: Listen to a piece of mariachi or flamenco music.

learn: Madrid (Spain), Ciudad de México, Buenos Aires (Argentina).
Lima (Peru), Bogotá (Colombia).
Santiago (Chile).
lessons.try: Label capitals on a map.

learn: Over 40 million people in the US speak Spanish at home.
Many place names are Spanish: Arizona, Nevada, Los Angeles.
Spanish is heard across the Southwest.
check: Over ___ million people in the US speak Spanish at home.
lessons.try: Find five Spanish place names near you.

learn: The Andes mountains run down South America.
The Amazon rainforest covers part of Peru, Colombia and more.
Spain is on the Iberian Peninsula.
lessons.try: Make a geography fact card.

learn: Frida Kahlo, painter from Mexico.
Miguel de Cervantes, writer from Spain.
Simón Bolívar, leader in South America.
lessons.try: Present a famous Spanish speaker.

learn: Nahuatl, Quechua and Guaraní are still spoken.
Spanish borrowed words: chocolate, tomate.
Guaraní is an official language of Paraguay.
lessons.try: Find three Spanish words from Nahuatl.

learn: Countries.
Festivals.
Art, music and food.
lessons.try: Travel poster for a Spanish-speaking country.
